text: The linewidth of a semiconductor laser exceeds the basic Schawlow-Townes value by a factor (1 + α_H²). What is the physical origin of this enhancement?
choices: The cavity photon lifetime is too short
Spontaneous emission is negligible in semiconductors
The mirror reflectivity is too high
Gain fluctuations couple to refractive-index fluctuations through the linewidth-enhancement (Henry) factor α_H ≈ 3–5
explanation: In semiconductors, carrier-density changes alter both gain and refractive index, so amplitude noise feeds into phase noise; this coupling is the Henry factor α_H ≈ 3–5, giving Δν = Δν_ST(1 + α_H²). Spontaneous emission is precisely what drives the linewidth (not negligible), and neither photon lifetime nor mirror reflectivity produces the (1 + α_H²) term.
